case: Reduce redundant defensive byte copies in a restore validation prefix
problem: A restore path copied an immutable byte holder for an equality comparison and separately copied each freshly loaded material twice for adjacent length and digest checks.
change: Compare the holder's private bytes through its existing read-only content comparison, avoiding an accessor clone. The caller-supplied saved-state encoder still executes at its original point on every replay.

After every fresh archive load, take one local defensive copy and use it for both length and digest checks. Keep the original length-first short circuit, so a length mismatch never invokes the digest.
preserved_contract: Every replay invokes the original saved-state encoder and freshly loads archive material; no encoded-state or material-qualification cache is introduced.
Exact byte comparison, material bounds, digest validation and original failure order remain in place.
Original manifest, state, session and canonical-entry gates, plus all later replay callbacks, retain their positions and checks.
Private byte ownership and defensive accessor behavior remain intact; no new public API, field, method or type is added.

software_evidence.implementation: Two edits within existing method bodies; owner-authored, independently source-reviewed.
software_evidence.test_origin: Six new public-prefix tests using a real read-only writer fixture and its issued session. Test review was nonblind to the candidate.
software_evidence.source_revision_history: Two earlier test revisions were corrected during source review before any test compilation. They were not compiler failures. The final revision was the first actually compiled and executed.
software_evidence.timing_scope: Sum of three recorded process durations; not an end-to-end benchmark or speed measurement.
coverage: Each replay reopens materials and checks the actual session before the external replay callback.
A second replay cannot reuse the first material qualification.
A mismatching saved state fails before the external callback.
A caller-supplied numeric subclass still observes saved-state encoding on every replay.
Wrong length performs no digest and stops before later material.
Matching length still hashes and rejects a wrong digest.
software_evidence.diagnostic: The successful test run also emitted a logging-manager initialization diagnostic; stderr was not empty.

proof_boundary: The tests exercise the public software validation prefix through the saved-state comparison and a sentinel immediately before the external replay callback. They do not establish a successful complete recovery, later manifest join or reducer behavior, a native frame, or live-system authority.
